name: Cheshire
description: Cheshire is a historic county in North West England known for its attractive countryside, agricultural landscapes and affluent villages and towns. It includes Chester and major settlements such as Crewe and Warrington, alongside historic estates and parts of the Peak District fringe.

places.name: Cheshire East
places.description: A district covering much of eastern Cheshire, including the historic town of Macclesfield and the market town of Nantwich, known for its Tudor black-and-white architecture and dairy farming heritage.

places.name: Cheshire West and Chester
places.description: A district covering the Roman walled city of Chester, with its distinctive black-and-white Tudor 'Rows' shopping galleries and a well-preserved medieval street plan.

places.name: Halton
places.description: A district in Cheshire covering the towns of Runcorn and Widnes, historically a centre of the chemical industry on the banks of the River Mersey.

places.name: Warrington
places.description: An industrial town in Cheshire on the River Mersey, historically a centre for wire and chemical manufacturing, now a growing commercial hub between Liverpool and Manchester.
